claim: CPU-count Tokio workers retain avoidable memory during standalone installs.
evidence: All 256 scored installs passed. Two workers reduced cold RSS in all 32 paired samples. Wall-time effects were mixed. The selected policy preserves explicit overrides and workspace defaults. Final candidate: cold RSS fell in 31 of 32 paired samples, with median paired savings of 96.83 MiB for T3, 82.96 MiB for Vite, 12.20 MiB for Sharp, and 11.80 MiB for Nest. All 512 scored installs succeeded. Cold wall medians changed by -10, -58, -16.5, and +18 ms respectively. Matched locks and critical installed artifacts passed.
coverage: Worker-policy unit tests, standalone cancellation and metadata-failure workflows, workspace workflows, and balanced wall/RSS benchmarks.

coverage: Workspace root/member and uncertain-context tests, repeated 240-member benchmark, and workspace workflows.
